issues.expected: The Power_Off event must be consumable from every operating state the system can occupy (HumanDrivingMode, AutoNavigating, AutoFinal, and by extension AutonomousMode as a composite scope), ensuring the system can always transition to Final regardless of its current mode.
issues.observed: Power_Off's sole declared consumer is transition:line:21 ([*]→FinalState), which is an initial-pseudostate edge not reachable from any operating state. Inspection-equivalent event_consumers shows Power_Off reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]. Verify fact event-consumer:Power_Off is refuted. No operating state (HumanDrivingMode, AutoNavigating, AutoFinal) has any outgoing transition triggered by Power_Off.
issues.reason: The derived contract requires event_consumer_coverage for Power_Off across all operating states. The deterministic facts conclusively show the only consumer is at the initial pseudostate level with zero reachable consumers from operating states. This is a W1 candidate because no frozen predicate directly expresses global event-consumer-coverage over a scope; the claim is precise and model-bound but falls outside the S1-S5/G1-G3/R1-R3/V1 registry for this property form.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The [*]→FinalState edge (line:21) is technically declared and the FinalState target is reachable from [*] per the reachability facts. A lenient reading might argue the system 'can' reach Final on Power_Off if it is at the initial point. However, the behavioral obligation is about operability: once the system has entered an operating state (after Power_On), Power_Off cannot be consumed to terminate. The verify fact explicitly refutes reachable consumer coverage.

decisions.basis: Supplied dossier: candidate NL-CONTRACT-NL5-ENDPOINT-1, complete FCSTM transition inventory (8 rows), binding element refs (state:HumanDrivingMode:line:8, state:FinalState:line:17, transition:line:21, event:Power_Off:line:7), source refs (llms_emp_feedback_final_0000.puml:line:14, tr_0006), verify_facts event-consumer:Power_Off refuted with reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[].
decisions.reason: The NL requirement 'when power off, it will transit to final state' demands a runtime transition from an operating state to FinalState on Power_Off. The complete FCSTM transition inventory (8 rows) confirms no transition has source=HumanDrivingMode (or any other operating state) with target=FinalState. The sole FinalState-incoming edge is transition:line:21 ([*]→FinalState, trigger=Power_Off), which is an initial-pseudostate entry edge valid only at system initialization under UML 2.5.1 §14.5.6.2, not a runtime handler. The candidate's strongest rebuttal—that this edge acts as a system-level global handler available from any context—is incompatible with standard UML initial-pseudostate semantics and is excluded by the exact model facts showing the edge's source is the initial pseudostate, not an operating state. No competent alternative reading survives.
decisions.violated_obligation: A transition from an operating state (e.g., HumanDrivingMode) to FinalState triggered by Power_Off must exist so the system can terminate from its current operating mode

decisions.basis: Supplied dossier: candidate NL-CONTRACT-NL5-DERIVED-ce5f8476b43be5c0e29e, deterministic event_consumer_fact (reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]), verify_fact event-consumer:Power_Off status=refuted, complete FCSTM transition inventory, binding element refs (event:Power_Off:line:7, states HumanDrivingMode:line:8, AutoNavigating:line:10, AutoFinal:line:11, FinalState:line:17, transition:line:21), source refs (llms_emp_feedback_final_0000.puml:line:14, tr_0006).
decisions.reason: The derived contract requires Power_Off to be consumable from all operating states. The deterministic event-consumer facts show reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] and the verify fact event-consumer:Power_Off is refuted. The complete FCSTM transition inventory confirms no transition from HumanDrivingMode, AutoNavigating, or AutoFinal triggers on Power_Off. The sole consumer (transition:line:21, [*]→FinalState) is an initial-pseudostate edge not reachable from any operating state during runtime.
